newsitem.title: USA: Heinz to cut 2,500 jobs, exit 4 businesses.
newsitem.headline: Heinz to cut 2,500 jobs, exit 4 businesses.

text.p: H.J. Heinz Co announced Friday a restructuring plan that includes closing or selling at least 25 plants worldwide, reducing its 43,000-strong workforce by 2,500, and exiting at least four non-strategic businesses.
Heinz said the restructuring would reduce its fiscal 1997 pre-tax earnings by $650 million.

It said it expects cash proceeds from the sale of plants and businesses to reach $750-$850 million. It said it had a letter of agreement to sell its Ore-Ida food service business to McCain Foods Ltd for about $500 million.

Heinz Chairman Tony O'Reilly, revealing details of the restructuring in an address to analysts in San Francisco, said, "This bold initiative (will) ride the global growth wave in terms of brand growth, financial performance and enhanced shareholder value."
The plan is designed to strengthen the company's six core businesses and improve profitability and global growth, Heinz said.
O'Reilly said the plan is designed to ensure 10-12 percent earnings growth into the next century, and boost sales to $14-$15 billion by 2003, from $9.5 billion in fiscal 1997.

O'Reilly said the restructuring should generate working capital reductions of $300 million within the next 12 months, yield pre-tax savings of about $120 million in fiscal 1998, and achieve over $2 billion in cash flow over the next five years, with $1 billion of that total coming in the next 12 months.
Heinz said the plan should increase its gross margin from 36 percent to 40 percent by fiscal 2001.
The company said that as a result of plant closures or sales, sales in the current fiscal fourth quarter ending April 30 will be flat compared with the year-earlier $2.5 billion.
Heinz did not specify which four businesses it would exit but said it would shed real estate in the United Kingdom and assets in New Zealand.

It did not specify which 25 plants would be sold or closed but said three seafood production facilities would be downsized or sold, and several production facilities in Australia and New Zealand would be closed.
O'Reilly said the growth plan will focus on investing in Heinz's big global brandsm including ketchup, tuna and pickles, and will maximize market share around the world.
He said products will be extended to new, growing markets, including Asia and Eastern Europe.
